results.title: Best Practices for Handling Missing Data in Data Analysis
results.content: # What are the best practices for identifying and handling missing data in your datasets? Why does missing data occur? How to identify missing data? How to handle missing data? Missing data is a common and inevitable problem in data analysis. Therefore, you need to know how to identify and handle missing data in your datasets effectively and efficiently. In this article, you will learn some best practices for dealing with missing data, such as:. ## 1 Why does missing data occur? Missing data is also sometimes not "missing" at all, but completely natural. ## 2 How to identify missing data? The first step in handling missing data is to identify its presence, extent, and type in your datasets. You can use descriptive statistics, visualizations, or specialized tools to explore and analyze your data for missing values. For example, you can use the isna() function in pandas to check for missing values in a dataframe, or the missingno library to create graphical summaries of missing data patterns. ## 3 How to handle missing data? Once you have identified the missing data in your datasets, you have to decide how to handle it. Deletion is a simple and straightforward way to handle missing data, but it also has some drawbacks. Deletion also assumes that the missing data is MCAR, which may not be true in many cases. Therefore, you should only use deletion when the amount of missing data is small and insignificant, and when the missing data is not related to your variables of interest. Imputation is a more complex and sophisticated way to handle missing data, but it also has some benefits. Imputation also allows you to handle different types of missing data, such as MAR or MNAR, by using different methods and assumptions. Therefore, you should use imputation when the amount of missing data is large and important, and when the missing data is related to your variables of interest. Spotting missing data is just step one. Multiple imputation is a strategy where statisticians create several sets of plausible values to fill in the missing data. Statisticians use this approach because it accounts for the missing values by utilizing the available data to estimate the probabilities of different outcomes. This method helps in constructing a complete dataset where the missing values are fitted in a way that reflects the structure of the data that is present. Dummy variable adjustment involves creating indicator variables that signal whether data for a particular observation is missing.
